title: Checking a car in
purpose: The counter's part of receiving a car: walk-round, mileage, the complaint, keys.
facts: Nine steps: walk-round with four corner photos; mileage from the dash (ERP mess kind 3); complaint in the customer's words with conditions; "anything else"; contact and who else may approve; the free inspection; keys tagged, wheel-lock key asked for; a time for the first call; order opened from the appointment with car and customer checked (mess kind 8).
No completion time is promised at check-in; a call time is.

list_items.item: Walk round it with the customer. Dents, scratches, cracked glass, warning lights on the dash: say them out loud and note them. Take four photos, one per corner.
Mileage off the dash, typed, not guessed. If it is lower than last time, look again; you have probably dropped a digit.
The complaint in their words, and when it happens: cold, hot, braking, turning, at speed. If they can, ride with the technician for the noise.
What they are not asking for. "Anything else it is doing?" You would be surprised.
How to reach them today, and until when. Text or call. Who else may approve work.
The inspection: tell them it is free and that they will get photos. Almost nobody says no.
Keys: tag with the order number, on the board. Wheel-lock key? Ask now, not when the wheels are coming off.
A time for the first call from us. "You will hear from me by eleven with what we found." Then they do.
Open the order from the appointment. Check it is the right car on the right customer.
